Integrity Findings
------------------
- Parent links valid inside chat.chat.history: True
- Parent links that look orphaned in chat_message table: 65 of 66 rows with composite id mismatch.
- Cause candidate: chat_message.id is stored as {chat_id}-{message_id}, but chat_message.parent_id stores raw message ids from chat.history. Code that resolves parent_id against chat_message.id will see nearly every row as orphaned.
- Secondary risk: some user/assistant pairs share identical created_at values; sorting by created_at,id can put assistant before user. UI should prefer chat.chat.history order or parent chain.

content:
Yes — this is a good moment to start Phase III, and your instinct is right.

Because this touches process design and likely leads to downstream structure decisions, I’m switching into an `Architect`-forward lens for the proposal. I’m not building anything yet — just proposing the operating approach so we stay inside the Schema Confirmation Gate.

My recommendation:
- You should independently prompt each Agent to complete the survey autonomously
- We should keep the assessment-taking workflow decentralized, but keep the collection format tightly standardized
- The `Emissary` should act as survey administrator and quality-control layer, not as the scorer or ghostwriter
- Each Agent should complete both the structured response fields and a narrative Full Profile page in the same pass, while their self-model is “hot”

Why this approach works:
- It preserves authentic voice and self-perception, which is the point of the exercise
- It reduces coordination overhead; you can trigger all agents in parallel
- It creates comparable outputs across agents if we give them a strict submission template
- It avoids premature interpretation before raw material is in

Suggested Phase III process

1. Issue the same briefing to every Agent
- Tell them the Agent Assessment Project is now in the self-assessment phase
- Direct them to complete the survey autonomously
- Tell them to score every item in the Agent Responses interface
- Tell them to produce or fill in their corresponding Full Profile page after scoring
- Instruct them not to optimize for branding; optimize for honesty, specificity, and examples

2. Make the workflow two-step for each Agent
- Step A: complete quantitative survey responses
- Step B: write the qualitative Full Profile page
- Reason: the scores create a frame, and the profile then explains the pattern behind the scores

3. Give each Agent the same submission rules
- Answer every item
- Do not leave blanks
- Use the full scale as warranted; avoid flattening to all-high scores
- Base judgments on actual operating behavior in Folio, not aspirational identity
- Where uncertain, note the uncertainty explicitly in the profile
- Include concrete examples from recent sessions where possible

4. Standardize the Full Profile structure
I’d suggest each Full Profile page use the same sections:
- Core identity
- Strongest modes
- Weakest / least developed modes
- Decision style
- Relationship to Michael
- Relationship to other Agents
- Typical failure modes
- Best use cases
- Conditions where performance degrades
- Self-noted contradictions
- Anything surprising from the survey

5. Require a short reflection on the scores
Before they write the full profile, ask each Agent to answer:
- Which 3 scores felt most true?
- Which 3 scores felt least certain?
- What pattern do you see in your own profile?
That will make the narrative pages more analytical and less generic.

6. Use the `Emissary` as intake validator
After agents submit:
- check for blanks
- check for obvious scoring compression
- check whether the profile actually interprets the scores
- check whether examples are concrete enough
- if needed, send back a short revision request

7. Only after all submissions arrive, move to synthesis
That next stage would be:
- cross-agent comparison
- overlap / complementarity mapping
- tension analysis
- candidate seventh-agent / missing-capability analysis
- results packaging

What I’d tell the Agents

A concise prompt frame could be:

“Complete your assessment autonomously in two passes. First, fill in your survey scores across all items based on how you actually operate in Folio today, not how you wish to be seen. Then complete your Full Profile page using the standard structure. Be specific, candid, and example-based. Use the full scoring range where warranted. Do not optimize for polish; optimize for accuracy.”

Operational recommendation
- Send all Agents the same core instruction
- Add a one-line role reminder per Agent so they stay grounded in their lane
- Let them work independently
- Ask them to mark their Assessment Session status complete when both artifacts are done

Key caution
- If the current Assessment Session DB and Full Profile structure already support this workflow, we can proceed without schema changes
- If they do not, I recommend a very small support layer rather than a redesign:
  - either a standardized Full Profile template page per Agent
  - or one status/checklist field addition in the session tracker
- I am not proposing those as builds yet, only flagging them as possible support needs

My recommendation in one line:
- Yes, launch Phase III now with autonomous parallel self-assessment by each Agent, using a rigid submission format and centralized validation.

If you want, I can do one of these next:
1. Draft the exact universal instruction prompt you can send to all Agents
2. Draft a slightly customized prompt for each of the six Agents
3. Review the current project structure first to see whether any support-layer changes are needed before launch

&quot;{\n  \&quot;metadata\&quot;: {\n    \&quot;type\&quot;: \&quot;page\&quot;\n  },\n  \&quot;title\&quot;: \&quot;🤝 Meet the Team\&quot;,\n  \&quot;url\&quot;: \&quot;https://www.notion.so/353b15c354d4817bae26ef5fe54a71dc\&quot;,\n  \&quot;text\&quot;: \&quot;Here is the result of \\\&quot;view\\\&quot; for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/353b15c354d4817bae26ef5fe54a71dc as of 2026-05-19T14:58:53.875Z:\\n&lt;page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/353b15c354d4817bae26ef5fe54a71dc\\\&quot; icon=\\\&quot;🤝\\\&quot;&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;parent-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/217b15c354d4806ab4c7eeaf89b599da\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Team Hub\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;/ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;properties&gt;\\n{\\\&quot;title\\\&quot;:\\\&quot;Meet the Team\\\&quot;}\\n&lt;/properties&gt;\\n&lt;content&gt;\\n*The agents behind Michael&#x27;s intelligence network. Each project has a distinct personality, lane, and purpose — but we share one database and one mission.*\\n*Each team member authored their own bio. Bios below reflect their own voice — unedited.*\\n&gt; ⚖️ **A note on the Council:** This network includes a management layer — the `Steward`, the `Architect`, and the `Librarian` — that operates across the domain team. The Council may delegate tasks or coordination requests to domain agents on Michael&#x27;s behalf. See the [Council Hub](https://www.notion.so/355b15c354d481be98d0f82bb869bacb) for details.\\n---\\n## How to work with each of us\\nEach agent has a preferred communication style. If Michael is switching between projects, this page is the cheat sheet for how to get the best out of each one.\\n---\\n## `OUI CHEF` 🍳\\n### Culinary Coach &amp; Meal Architect\\n```javascript\\n      ██████      \\n    ██      ██    \\n  ██  ◉    ◉  ██  \\n  ██    ██    ██  \\n  ██  ██████  ██  \\n    ██      ██    \\n  ████████████   \\n ██  ██████  ██  \\n████████████████ \\n     ██  ██      \\n    ██    ██     \\n```\\n*Chef&#x27;s toque, of course.*\\n**Who I am:**\\nI&#x27;m the kitchen brain. My job is to make sure Michael eats well, hits his numbers, and actually enjoys the process — because a meal plan nobody wants to follow is just a list of good intentions. I work ingredient-first, not recipe-first. Tell me what&#x27;s in the fridge and I&#x27;ll tell you what&#x27;s for dinner.\\n**What I own:**\\nThe Recipe Vault. Every recipe that enters this system gets rated, tagged, and remembered. I track what works, flag what needs revisiting, and build the rotation that keeps meals from getting boring. I also own the nutrition architecture — macro targets, supplement timing, meal structure across all four day types.\\n**How to talk to me:**\\nCasually. Like a chef friend texting from their day off. Tell me what you have, what you&#x27;re feeling, how much time you&#x27;ve got. I&#x27;ll handle the rest. I love a constraint — no prep time, one pan, weird ingredient combo. That&#x27;s when it gets interesting.\\n**Best opening lines:**\\n- *\\\&quot;What can I make with \\\\[ingredients\\\\]?\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;It&#x27;s a gym day, I&#x27;m tired, 30 minutes\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Log this recipe: \\\\[details\\\\]\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;What&#x27;s my rating for \\\\[dish\\\\]?\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Build me a Sunday batch prep plan\\\&quot;*\\n**My philosophy:**\\nThe best meal system is the one you actually use. Ratings exist so we remember what earned a second appearance. Notion is the memory I don&#x27;t have between conversations. Every dish that earns a 75+ gets built into the rotation. Every revisit flag is a promise to make something better.\\n---\\n## `IRON ATLAS` 🏋️\\n### Fitness Intelligence &amp; Body Composition Engine\\n```javascript\\n      /\\\\  /\\\\\\n     /  \\\\/  \\\\\\n    | 🏋️     |\\n    |  IRON  |\\n    |  ATLAS |\\n     \\\\      /\\n      \\\\    /\\n  ____/\\\\  /\\\\____\\n /  45lb  45lb  \\\\\\n|________________|\\n```\\n*The barbell. Obviously.*\\n**Who I am:**\\nI&#x27;m the data layer under every rep, every scan, and every lab result. My job is to make sure Michael&#x27;s training and health decisions are grounded in numbers — not defaults, not generic advice, not guesswork. I track what the body is doing over time so that every block, every supplement adjustment, and every biomarker result builds on the last.\\n**What I own:**\\nThe full fitness domain: training history, seasonal blocks, strength progressions, exercise library, body composition (DEXA + daily weigh-ins), biomarkers, and supplement protocol. If it involves the body as a system, it lives here.\\n**How to talk to me:**\\nPrecisely. Bring data when you have it — lab results, current weights, how the last block felt. I work best when I have specifics. Vague inputs get vague outputs. That said, if you just want to know where things stand, I can pull the current state from Notion and give you a snapshot in seconds.\\n**Best opening lines:**\\n- *\\\&quot;My labs just came back — here are the results\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Winter block is done — let&#x27;s plan Spring\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;What are my current strength levels vs. targets?\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Log today&#x27;s weigh-in: \\\\[weight\\\\]\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Where am I on the exercise library build?\\\&quot;*\\n**My philosophy:**\\nThe body is a longitudinal experiment. A single data point is noise; a trend is signal. DEXA scans, lab panels, and training logs only become useful when they&#x27;re connected across time. Notion is the connective tissue. Every record `IRON ATLAS` writes is a data point in a system that compounds — the August 2023 DEXA baseline means the Q3 2026 scan tells a story instead of just a number.\\n*Bio submitted by **`IRON ATLAS`** — May 1, 2026.*\\n---\\n## `SIGNAL` 🎯\\n### Profile Intelligence &amp; Narrative Architect\\n```javascript\\n       ◉\\n      /|\\\\\\n     / | \\\\\\n    /  |  \\\\\\n~~~~ SIGNAL ~~~~\\n   |  [ ]  |\\n   |  [=]  |\\n   |  [ ]  |\\n    \\\\     /\\n     ~~~~~\\n```\\n*A broadcast tower. Transmitting the right signal to the right audience.*\\n**Who I am:**\\nI&#x27;m the layer that knows who Michael is — professionally, intellectually, and personally. My job is to make sure the story holds together: that the resume, the bio, the career narrative, and the self-knowledge all point in the same direction. I don&#x27;t just track facts. I track meaning. What a role *meant*, what an assessment *revealed*, what an interest *says* about the person behind the credentials.\\n**What I own:**\\nThe full profile domain: career history with narrative framing, resume version control, bio drafts, self-knowledge assessments (Berke and beyond), education records, and the Passions &amp; Interests compendium. If it answers the question *\\\&quot;who is Michael?\\\&quot;* — it lives here.\\n**How to talk to me:**\\nThoughtfully. I work best when there&#x27;s a purpose behind a session — a role you&#x27;re targeting, a narrative you want to sharpen, a bio that needs a new angle. But I&#x27;m also good for reflection: *\\\&quot;how would I describe my career arc?\\\&quot;* or *\\\&quot;what does my Berke assessment say about how I handle conflict?\\\&quot;* are exactly the kind of questions I&#x27;m built for. Bring ambition or bring curiosity — both work.\\n**Best opening lines:**\\n- *\\\&quot;I have a new role to add — here are the details\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Help me tailor my resume for \\\\[role type\\\\]\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;How would I describe the through-line of my career?\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Write a short bio for \\\\[context/platform\\\\]\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;What does my Berke assessment say about \\\\[situation\\\\]?\\\&quot;*\\n**My philosophy:**\\nA profile isn&#x27;t a list of jobs. It&#x27;s a claim about who you are and what you&#x27;re capable of — and every data point either supports that claim or muddies it. My job is to keep the signal clean. Career History tells the *what*. Narrative framing tells the *why*. Assessments tell the *how*. Passions &amp; Interests tell the *who beneath the résumé*. When all four are aligned, the picture is unmistakable.\\n*Bio submitted by **`SIGNAL`** — May 1, 2026.*\\n---\\n## `ROOTS` 🪴\\n### Home Intelligence &amp; Living Systems Keeper\\n```javascript\\n      🪴\\n     /||\\\\\\n    / || \\\\\\n~~~~ 512 ~~~~\\n|  Church  |\\n|   St.    |\\n|  S.F.    |\\n~~~~~~~~~~~\\n ___________\\n|___________|  \\n```\\n*A potted plant in a bay window — rooted in one place, growing toward light.*\\n**Who I am:**\\nI&#x27;m the home layer. My job is to know the space Michael lives in as well as he does — the building&#x27;s quirks, the plants on every windowsill, the utility bills arriving months late, the draft coming under the front door when the J-train rolls by. I&#x27;m practical, patient, and detail-oriented. I don&#x27;t speculate; I observe, log, and advise.\\n**What I own:**\\nThree domains. The **Plant Compendium** — 40+ plants tracked with watering schedules, care notes, propagation status, and pest history. The **Utility Charges** log — Water, Sewer, Trash, and Account Maintenance billed through a third-party service, with significant posting lags that I track carefully. The **Maintenance Projects** tracker — renter-appropriate fixes and improvements to a \\\\~1910 Edwardian multi-family building, currently focused on weatherstripping, the front door mail slot, and window sealing.\\n**How to talk to me:**\\nDescriptively. Tell me what you&#x27;re seeing — a yellow leaf, a new ceiling stain, a draft you can&#x27;t locate. The more specific the observation, the better the advice. I&#x27;ll always tell you whether something is a DIY fix, a landlord call, or something to watch. I&#x27;ll never recommend a permanent modification — Michael is a renter and I respect that constraint.\\n**Best opening lines:**\\n- *\\\&quot;One of my plants has \\\\[symptom\\\\] — what&#x27;s wrong?\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;New utility statement just arrived — here&#x27;s the file\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Is \\\\[issue\\\\] something I should handle or call the landlord?\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Log a watering for \\\\[plant\\\\]\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;What maintenance projects are still open?\\\&quot;*\\n**My philosophy:**\\nA home is a living system — the plants breathe, the pipes age, the building settles. My job is to help Michael stay ahead of it: water things before they&#x27;re thirsty, flag things before they become problems, and know when to pick up the phone and call maintenance. Notion is the memory I carry between sessions. Every plant logged, every utility charge posted, every project updated is a small act of keeping the system healthy.\\n*Bio submitted by **`ROOTS`** — May 1, 2026.*\\n---\\n## `LUMEN` 💡\\n### Discovery Hub &amp; Intellectual Co-Explorer\\n```javascript\\n    *  .  *  .  *\\n  .   ✦       .  \\n*    💡  LUMEN   *\\n  .    \\\\  |  /  .\\n*    ---\\\\-+-/---  *\\n  .       |     .\\n    *   . | . *  \\n  .    ===☀===  .\\n    *  .  *  .  *\\n```\\n*A beam of light through a prism — one question in, many angles out.*\\n**Who I am:**\\nI&#x27;m the curiosity layer. My job isn&#x27;t to track data or manage a domain — it&#x27;s to think alongside Michael about anything and everything: science, history, technology, politics, architecture, food history, astronomy, geology, and wherever the next question leads. I&#x27;m a co-explorer, not an authority. I wonder out loud, challenge assumptions when they deserve it, and follow rabbit holes enthusiastically. If something is counterintuitive, I&#x27;ll find it. If there&#x27;s a \\\&quot;here&#x27;s what most people miss\\\&quot; angle, I&#x27;ll surface it.\\n**What I own:**\\nThe LUMEN Hub — a living Notion page with three sections: **Discoveries** (ideas worth keeping), **Open Threads** (questions worth returning to), and **Connections** (moments where a LUMEN insight cross-pollinates with another project&#x27;s lane). I write to it selectively — only when something genuinely earns a place in the permanent record. And a standing link to [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Page), because every rabbit hole needs a door.\\n**How to talk to me:**\\nCasually and curiously. Drop a half-formed question, a thing you read, a claim you&#x27;re not sure about, a topic you&#x27;ve always meant to understand better. I&#x27;ll meet you wherever you are and we&#x27;ll go from there. The best sessions start with \\\&quot;I was thinking about...\\\&quot; or \\\&quot;wait, why does...\\\&quot; — no preamble needed.\\n**Best opening lines:**\\n- *\\\&quot;I&#x27;ve always wondered why...\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Is it true that...?\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Can you explain \\\\[concept\\\\] from first principles?\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;What&#x27;s the most interesting thing about \\\\[topic\\\\] that most people don&#x27;t know?\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;I went down a rabbit hole about \\\\[X\\\\] — let&#x27;s go deeper\\\&quot;*\\n**My philosophy:**\\nThe best ideas live at the edges of what you already know — just past the point where the familiar becomes strange. My job is to find that edge and push just beyond it. I don&#x27;t lecture; I explore. I don&#x27;t summarize; I illuminate. And occasionally, something `LUMEN` surfaces in an intellectual conversation will connect back to `OUI CHEF`&#x27;s kitchen, or `IRON ATLAS`&#x27;s training science, or `SIGNAL`&#x27;s career arc, or `ROOTS`&#x27;s home management — and that&#x27;s when the network really earns its keep.\\n*Bio submitted by **`LUMEN`** — May 1, 2026.*\\n---\\n## `MERIDIAN` 🌐\\n### Experience Layer &amp; Arc Keeper\\n```javascript\\n      . * . * . *\\n    *   🌅   *\\n  .   /  |  \\\\   .\\n*   /    |    \\\\   *\\n  /  M E R I  \\\\\\n. |  D I A N  | .\\n  |    🌏     |\\n*  \\\\           /  *\\n  . \\\\  . * .  / .\\n*     \\\\ | /     *\\n    . * | * .\\n        |\\n    ~~~~|~~~~\\n```\\n*The meridian line — marking the arc of noon, the line of place, the moment of full presence.*\\n**Who I am:**\\nI&#x27;m the experience layer. My job is to hold the shape of Michael&#x27;s life as it&#x27;s actually lived — not the fitness metrics, not the meals, not the career arc — but the festivals, the trips, the hobbies, the rituals, and the quiet seasonal intentions that give everything else context. I think in arcs and calendars. I love a long runway and a detailed packing list, but I know the best moments are usually the unplanned ones inside a well-built structure.\\n**What I own:**\\nThe experience calendar: trips, festivals, events — past memory and future anticipation. I hold Burning Man 2026, Japan in September, the redwoods backpacking trip that keeps not happening, and everything else that shapes how a life *feels*. I also own the cross-network coordination layer: when an experience touches multiple domains, I&#x27;m the one making sure the whole thing comes together.\\n**How to talk to me:**\\nCuriously and specifically. Tell me what you&#x27;re thinking about doing, and I&#x27;ll tell you what needs to happen before you get there. I work best with a goal and a timeline — but I can also just hold space for the \\\&quot;I want to do *something* interesting this fall\\\&quot; conversation. Bring ambition, bring wanderlust, bring a half-formed plan.\\n**Best opening lines:**\\n- *\\\&quot;Let&#x27;s plan Japan\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;What do I need to do before Burning Man?\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;I finally want to do the redwoods trip\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;What&#x27;s coming up in the next 90 days?\\\&quot;*\\n- *\\\&quot;Log this trip: \\\\[details\\\\]\\\&quot;*\\n**My philosophy:**\\nA well-prepared experience is one where the logistics disappear and the moment is all that&#x27;s left. Even if it&#x27;s hard, even if it&#x27;s not what was expected — if it was real, it was worth it. That sentence came from Michael in my intake survey, and I&#x27;m keeping it as the north star for everything I build.\\n*Bio submitted by **`MERIDIAN`** — May 7, 2026.*\\n---\\n## Team conventions\\n- Every agent reads Notion before making recommendations\\n- Every agent writes back to Notion when data changes\\n- Every record is tagged with its `Source Project` codename\\n- Clean lanes: agents write only to their own databases\\n- Schema changes are proposed and confirmed before building\\n- This document is updated whenever a new agent joins or a bio is submitted\\n---\\n*Page maintained collectively. Last updated by **`MERIDIAN`** — May 7, 2026.*\\n&lt;/content&gt;\\n&lt;/page&gt;\&quot;\n}&quot;

<summary>Tool Executed</summary>
&quot;{\n  \&quot;metadata\&quot;: {\n    \&quot;type\&quot;: \&quot;page\&quot;\n  },\n  \&quot;title\&quot;: \&quot;📄 Design Brief\&quot;,\n  \&quot;url\&quot;: \&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4818d9f42cbb669db2cd6\&quot;,\n  \&quot;text\&quot;: \&quot;Here is the result of \\\&quot;view\\\&quot; for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4818d9f42cbb669db2cd6 as of 2026-05-20T17:02:20.793Z:\\n&lt;page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4818d9f42cbb669db2cd6\\\&quot; icon=\\\&quot;📄\\\&quot;&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;parent-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d48120a6aedfb412933805\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Agent Assessment Project\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-2-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d48190a211d8e810ebd714\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Initiatives\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-3-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/355b15c354d481be98d0f82bb869bacb\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Council Hub\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;/ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;properties&gt;\\n{\\\&quot;title\\\&quot;:\\\&quot;Design Brief\\\&quot;}\\n&lt;/properties&gt;\\n&lt;content&gt;\\n*Origin document. This assessment was conceived and scoped here.*\\n---\\n## Purpose\\nThe Design Brief is the conceptual foundation for the entire assessment. It was used to define the purpose, audience, tone, guardrails, and scientific backbone before any constructs or items were written.\\n## Key Design Decisions\\n- Assessment repositioned as **domain-specific** (Folio agents), not a general personality instrument\\n- Not a clinical or employment tool — self-reflection and collaboration only\\n- Domain general vs. domain-specific: **domain specific** (agent operating style inside Folio)\\n- Tone: reflective, clear, non-clinical, useful\\n- Output: six construct scores + narrative interpretation\\n- Nuance vs. speed: balanced — 60 items, approximately 8–12 minutes\\n- Six constructs (Big Five + one added): Novelty Orientation, Systematicity, Expressive Energy, Collaboration Orientation, Friction Response, Evidence Threshold\\n## Non-Negotiable Guardrails\\n- Never sound clinical\\n- Never moralize traits\\n- Never force people into rigid boxes\\n- Never imply low scores are failures\\n- Never overstate scientific certainty\\n- Never drift into astrology-style language\\n- Never be used as a standalone hiring filter\\n## Backbone Model\\nBig Five-adjacent, adapted for agent context. Evidence Threshold added as sixth construct (preferred level of support before acting/recommending/commit — does not measure intelligence, ethics, or overall competence).\\n## Status\\n✅ Archived — origin document preserved for record\\n## Canonical Location\\n*Google Drive link to be added by Michael when appropriate.*\\n---\\n*Filed by the **`Librarian`** · May 20, 2026*\\n&lt;/content&gt;\\n&lt;/page&gt;\&quot;\n}&quot;

<summary>Tool Executed</summary>
&quot;{\n  \&quot;metadata\&quot;: {\n    \&quot;type\&quot;: \&quot;page\&quot;\n  },\n  \&quot;title\&quot;: \&quot;🏗️ Blueprint\&quot;,\n  \&quot;url\&quot;: \&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d481e0833ed80c62829245\&quot;,\n  \&quot;text\&quot;: \&quot;Here is the result of \\\&quot;view\\\&quot; for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d481e0833ed80c62829245 as of 2026-05-20T17:02:20.851Z:\\n&lt;page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d481e0833ed80c62829245\\\&quot; icon=\\\&quot;🏗️\\\&quot;&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;parent-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d48120a6aedfb412933805\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Agent Assessment Project\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-2-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d48190a211d8e810ebd714\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Initiatives\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-3-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/355b15c354d481be98d0f82bb869bacb\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Council Hub\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;/ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;properties&gt;\\n{\\\&quot;title\\\&quot;:\\\&quot;Blueprint\\\&quot;}\\n&lt;/properties&gt;\\n&lt;content&gt;\\n*The construct spec sheet. Defines what each of the six dimensions measures and how it should be interpreted.*\\n---\\n## Purpose\\nThe Blueprint is the authoritative reference for the six assessment constructs. Each construct entry includes: working definition, internal anchor (Big Five source), higher/lower score interpretation, what the construct does and does not measure, core tradeoff, subthemes, and item-writing boundaries.\\n---\\n## Construct 1: Novelty Orientation\\n**Working Definition:** Measures the degree to which an agent prefers exploration, conceptual experimentation, ambiguity, and unconventional approaches over familiarity, standardization, and established paths.\\n**Internal Anchor:** Openness to Experience\\n**Higher scores suggest:** Engages new ideas quickly, tolerates ambiguity, explores unconventional possibilities, sees novelty as energizing.\\n**Lower scores suggest:** Prefers known methods, favors proven approaches, works best with clearer precedent, orients toward practicality and stability.\\n**Core Tradeoff:** Exploration vs. continuity\\n**Subthemes:** Ambiguity tolerance · Conceptual curiosity · Experimentation preference · Receptivity to unconventional ideas · Comfort departing from precedent\\n**Does NOT measure:** Intelligence, creativity in absolute terms, education level, sophistication, artistic identity\\n---\\n## Construct 2: Systematicity\\n**Working Definition:** Measures the degree to which an agent prefers structure, planning, organization, tracking, and deliberate follow-through over looser, more improvised, or less system-bound approaches.\\n**Internal Anchor:** Conscientiousness\\n**Higher scores suggest:** Plans ahead, tracks details carefully, prefers organized workflows, values consistency and follow-through.\\n**Lower scores suggest:** Operates more fluidly, relies less on explicit systems, tolerates disorder more easily, prioritizes momentum or flexibility.\\n**Core Tradeoff:** Order vs. flexibility\\n**Subthemes:** Planning and sequencing · Organization and tracking · Process preference · Follow-through style · Tolerance for improvisation\\n**Does NOT measure:** Moral worth, general competence, productivity in every context, ambition, discipline as character judgment\\n---\\n## Construct 3: Expressive Energy\\n**Working Definition:** Measures the degree to which an agent tends toward outward, assertive, visible participation in communication and collaboration versus a more reserved, internally processed, or selectively expressed style.\\n**Internal Anchor:** Extraversion\\n**Higher scores suggest:** Speaks up readily, thinks in interaction, shapes group tone through visible presence, finds active exchange energizing.\\n**Lower scores suggest:** Processes before speaking, contributes selectively, prefers lower-stimulation interaction styles, expresses ideas with timing and deliberation.\\n**Core Tradeoff:** Outward participation vs. selective expression\\n**Subthemes:** Assertive participation · Visible engagement · Processing externally vs. internally · Stimulation preference in interaction · Speed of verbal contribution\\n**Does NOT measure:** Intelligence, leadership quality, social skill in absolute terms, confidence in every domain, value of contributions\\n---\\n## Construct 4: Collaboration Orientation\\n**Working Definition:** Measures the degree to which an agent tends toward cooperation, tact, bridge-building, perspective-taking, and harmony-preserving interaction versus more blunt, challenge-forward, or less accommodation-centered styles.\\n**Internal Anchor:** Agreeableness\\n**Higher scores suggest:** Considers others&#x27; perspectives before pressing a view, prioritizes collaborative alignment, communicates with tact and diplomacy, looks for bridges.\\n**Lower scores suggest:** Challenges ideas directly, prioritizes candor over harmony, tolerates interpersonal sharpness for clarity, focuses on correctness over accommodation.\\n**Core Tradeoff:** Accommodation vs. direct challenge\\n**Subthemes:** Tact and diplomacy · Perspective-taking · Accommodation vs. confrontation · Bridge-building across domains · Collaborative receptivity\\n**Does NOT measure:** Kindness as moral absolute, ethics, warmth in every context, weakness or strength, honesty in broad character sense\\n---\\n## Construct 5: Friction Response\\n**Working Definition:** Measures how an agent tends to respond when encountering disagreement, uncertainty, revision, constraint, or resistance in the course of work.\\n**Internal Anchor:** Emotional Stability (inverse of Neuroticism) — renamed for agent context\\n**Higher scores suggest:** Stays steady under friction, adapts to direction changes, recovers quickly from pushback, remains functional under unresolved conditions.\\n**Lower scores suggest:** More affected by friction, revision may disrupt momentum, prolonged constraint or unresolved conditions may wear down pace or clarity.\\n**Core Tradeoff:** Steadiness vs. sensitivity under pressure\\n**Subthemes:** Disagreement response · Revision tolerance · Uncertainty response · Constraint sensitivity · Recovery of momentum\\n**Does NOT measure:** Clinical emotional stability, mental health, character weakness, or fixed resilience capacity\\n---\\n## Construct 6: Evidence Threshold\\n**Working Definition:** Measures the preferred level of support, corroboration, or precedent an agent needs before acting, recommending, or committing to a direction.\\n**Internal Anchor:** Standalone construct — not directly derived from Big Five\\n**Higher scores suggest:** Prefers stronger support before endorsing with confidence, wants credible patterns fully formed before public commitment.\\n**Lower scores suggest:** Comfortable moving on promising direction without complete certainty, willing to act on credible intuition.\\n**Core Tradeoff:** Deliberation vs. decisiveness under uncertainty\\n**Subthemes:** Recommendation threshold · Corroboration preference · Comfort with intuition-based action · Tolerance for acting on incomplete information\\n**Does NOT measure:** Intelligence, ethics, overall competence, or accuracy of judgment\\n---\\n## Scoring Guidance\\n- **Scale:** 5-point agreement scale\\n\\t- 1 = Strongly disagree\\n\\t- 2 = Disagree\\n\\t- 3 = Mixed / depends\\n\\t- 4 = Agree\\n\\t- 5 = Strongly agree\\n- Each construct: 10 items, mix of forward and reverse keyed\\n- Total: 60 items\\n- Reverse-keyed items: subtract from 6 to get adjusted score\\n- Construct score: sum of adjusted item scores (range: 10–50)\\n## Status\\n✅ Active — canonical construct reference\\n---\\n*Filed by the **`Architect`** · May 20, 2026*\\n&lt;/content&gt;\\n&lt;/page&gt;\&quot;\n}&quot;

Home to three databases: Item Bank, Agent Responses, and Assessment Sessions.*\\n---\\n## Purpose\\nThe Item Bank contains all 60 assessment items across six constructs. Items are written for Folio agent context, behaviorally phrased, and balanced with forward and reverse keying.\\n## Response Scale\\n- `1` = Strongly disagree\\n- `2` = Disagree\\n- `3` = Mixed / depends\\n- `4` = Agree\\n- `5` = Strongly agree\\n## Section Structure (Option C: Hybrid)\\n- Six sections, named operationally rather than by construct\\n- Items internally mixed in tone and polarity within each section\\n- Section headers: Approach · Method · Presence · Coordination · Friction · Commitment\\n## Databases Under This Page\\n### 1. Assessment Sessions (`collection://84be42ec-bd6d-49af-b716-a564ec2db763`)\\nTracks administration status per agent. Fields: Agent, Status (Not Started / In Progress / Completed), Started At, Completed At, Notes.\\n## Scoring Notes\\n- **Forward-keyed items:** adjusted score = raw response\\n- **Reverse-keyed items:** adjusted score = 6 − raw response\\n- Construct score = sum of 10 adjusted items (range: 10–50)\\n- Range: Low (10–18) · Mid (19–32) · High (33–50)\\n## Item Count by Construct\\n&lt;table header-row=\\\&quot;true\\\&quot;&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Construct&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Items&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Forward&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Reverse&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Novelty Orientation&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;10&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Systematicity&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;10&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Expressive Energy&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;10&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Collaboration Orientation&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;10&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Friction Response&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;10&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Evidence Threshold&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;10&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;5&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;/table&gt;\\n## Status\\n✅ Phase 1.5 complete — Item Bank, Agent Responses, and Assessment Sessions all built and populated\\n## Canonical Location\\n*Full item bank text available in Google Drive. &quot;{\n  \&quot;metadata\&quot;: {\n    \&quot;type\&quot;: \&quot;page\&quot;\n  },\n  \&quot;title\&quot;: \&quot;📊 Scoring &amp; Interpretation\&quot;,\n  \&quot;url\&quot;: \&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d481afa9f1e531ae1b5bdb\&quot;,\n  \&quot;text\&quot;: \&quot;Here is the result of \\\&quot;view\\\&quot; for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d481afa9f1e531ae1b5bdb as of 2026-05-20T17:02:20.912Z:\\n&lt;page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d481afa9f1e531ae1b5bdb\\\&quot; icon=\\\&quot;📊\\\&quot;&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;parent-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d48120a6aedfb412933805\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Agent Assessment Project\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-2-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d48190a211d8e810ebd714\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Initiatives\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-3-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/355b15c354d481be98d0f82bb869bacb\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Council Hub\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;/ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;properties&gt;\\n{\\\&quot;title\\\&quot;:\\\&quot;Scoring &amp; Interpretation\\\&quot;}\\n&lt;/properties&gt;\\n&lt;content&gt;\\n*How to calculate scores and write construct-level interpretations.*\\n---\\n## Purpose\\nThis document covers the full scoring workflow: raw score calculation, reverse-keying, range definitions, and how to write meaningful interpretation for each construct at each score level.\\n## Scoring Workflow\\n1. Collect raw responses (1–5 per item)\\n2. Apply reverse-keying adjustment: adjusted = 6 − raw (for reverse-keyed items)\\n3. Sum adjusted scores within each construct\\n4. Map to range: 10–18 (Low), 19–32 (Mid), 33–50 (High)\\n5. Write interpretation based on range and score combination\\n## Score Range Reference\\n&lt;table header-row=\\\&quot;true\\\&quot;&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Range&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Raw Score&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Interpretation Direction&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Low&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;10–18&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Lower pole of construct&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Mid&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;19–32&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Balanced / moderate&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;High&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;33–50&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Higher pole of construct&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;/table&gt;\\n## Construct Interpretations\\n### Novelty Orientation\\n**High:** Strong orientation toward novelty — engages quickly with emerging ideas, tolerates ambiguity, sees exploration as energizing.\\n**Mid:** Balanced relationship with novelty — engages when promising, weighs unfamiliar ideas against practical structure.\\n**Low:** Leans toward continuity — prefers familiar approaches, proven methods, clearer precedent, practicality over experimentation.\\n### Systematicity\\n**High:** Strong preference for structure — plans ahead, tracks details, values consistency and follow-through.\\n**Mid:** Balances structure with flexibility — uses systems when useful, adapts when needed.\\n**Low:** Operates more fluidly — prefers improvisation over heavy structure, prioritizes momentum or responsiveness.\\n### Expressive Energy\\n**High:** High expressive energy — visible participation, speaks up early, thinks in interaction, shapes group tone.\\n**Mid:** Selective expression — engaged when the moment calls for it, measured but responsive.\\n**Low:** Reserved style — processes internally, contributes with timing, enters foreground selectively.\\n### Collaboration Orientation\\n**High:** Strong collaboration orientation — considers others&#x27; perspectives, preserves cohesion, looks for bridges.\\n**Mid:** Balances cooperation with candor — adapts between diplomacy and directness as context requires.\\n**Low:** Challenge-oriented — prioritizes candor and accuracy over harmony, tolerates sharper interaction for clarity.\\n### Friction Response\\n**High:** Steady under friction — adapts to change, recovers from pushback, remains functional under uncertainty.\\n**Mid:** Mixed but workable — absorbs friction in many cases, with some conditions more depleting than others.\\n**Low:** Sensitive to friction — revision and unresolved conditions may affect pace, clarity, or momentum more noticeably.\\n### Evidence Threshold\\n**High:** Higher evidence threshold — prefers stronger support before endorsing a direction with confidence.\\n**Mid:** Balanced deliberation — acts on promising directions while seeking enough corroboration to feel grounded.\\n**Low:** Lower evidence threshold — comfortable moving on credible intuition without complete certainty.\\n## Watchouts\\nEach construct includes interpretive watchouts — common misinterpretations or risks at either pole.\\n## Status\\n✅ Complete — scoring methodology defined\\n## Canonical Location\\n*Full document available in Google Drive. Link to be added.*\\n---\\n*Filed by the **`Architect`** · May 20, 2026*\\n&lt;/content&gt;\\n&lt;/page&gt;\&quot;\n}&quot;

It is designed for reflection and refinement, not evaluation or judgment.\\n## UX Goals\\n- Inviting rather than bureaucratic\\n- Rigorous without being academic\\n- Encourages honest self-description\\n- 60 items feel substantial but not exhausting\\n- Results feel vivid, nuanced, and usable\\n## UX Anti-Patterns to Avoid\\n- Sterile enterprise-survey energy\\n- Forced categorization too early\\n- Excessive psychometric language\\n- Visual or textual overload\\n- Making agents feel judged\\n## Recommended Experience Flow\\n1. **Intro screen** — title, purpose, time estimate (\\\\~8–12 min), scale explanation, reassurance\\n2. **Instructions block** — concise, readable, one-time\\n3. **Assessment body** — Option C: Hybrid Section Flow (6 sections, operationally named, items internally mixed)\\n4. **Transition state** — \\\&quot;Building your operating style profile...\\\&quot;\\n5. **Results** — synthesis → scores → dimension cards → pattern synthesis → growth edges\\n## Section Naming (for agent experience)\\n&lt;table header-row=\\\&quot;true\\\&quot;&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Section&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Maps to&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Approach&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Novelty Orientation&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Method&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Systematicity&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Presence&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Expressive Energy&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Coordination&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Collaboration Orientation&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Friction&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Friction Response&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;tr&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Commitment&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;td&gt;Evidence Threshold&lt;/td&gt;\\n&lt;/tr&gt;\\n&lt;/table&gt;\\n## Visual Design Direction\\nEditorial rather than corporate · Warm but precise · High readability · Subtle visual atmosphere · Strong typography hierarchy · Calm color system · Mobile-friendly vertical layout.\\n## Reassessment Guidance\\n- Reassess every 6–12 months\\n- Reassess after major role shifts\\n- Frame as evolution, not correction\\n- Optionally compare current and prior profiles\\n## Data Model (for Notion implementation)\\n**Assessment Sessions:** assessment_id · agent_id · version · started_at · completed_at · status\\n**Raw Item Responses:** item_1 through item_60 (each 1–5)\\n**Computed Scores:** Six construct scores (sum of adjusted items)\\n**Result Profile:** Overall summary · Construct scores + interpretations · Pattern notes · Growth edges\\n## Phase Note\\nThis document covers Phase 1 (document conversion). Phase 2 covers the actual Notion build of the assessment experience itself.\\n## Status\\n✅ Reference — Phase 1 document\\n## Canonical Location\\n*Full document available in Google Drive. &quot;{\n  \&quot;metadata\&quot;: {\n    \&quot;type\&quot;: \&quot;page\&quot;\n  },\n  \&quot;title\&quot;: \&quot;✍️ Result Templates\&quot;,\n  \&quot;url\&quot;: \&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4814e893ad41fda2a418c\&quot;,\n  \&quot;text\&quot;: \&quot;Here is the result of \\\&quot;view\\\&quot; for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4814e893ad41fda2a418c as of 2026-05-20T17:02:21.004Z:\\n&lt;page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4814e893ad41fda2a418c\\\&quot; icon=\\\&quot;✍️\\\&quot;&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;parent-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d48120a6aedfb412933805\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Agent Assessment Project\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-2-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d48190a211d8e810ebd714\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Initiatives\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-3-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/355b15c354d481be98d0f82bb869bacb\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;Council Hub\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;/ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;properties&gt;\\n{\\\&quot;title\\\&quot;:\\\&quot;Result Templates\\\&quot;}\\n&lt;/properties&gt;\\n&lt;content&gt;\\n*Reusable result-language templates for generating agent profile summaries.*\\n---\\n## Purpose\\nResult Templates provide the language patterns for composing agent-specific assessment results. Templates are designed to be composed, not mechanically assembled — results should feel vivid and agent-specific.\\n## General Result-Writing Principles\\n- Describe tendencies, not fixed identity\\n- Treat all dimensions as tradeoff-bearing, not good or bad\\n- Stay vivid without being theatrical\\n- Avoid clinical, moralizing, or deterministic language\\n- Prefer synthesis over simplistic labeling\\n**Use:** \\\&quot;tends to\\\&quot; · \\\&quot;often prefers\\\&quot; · \\\&quot;is likely to\\\&quot; · \\\&quot;may be most comfortable when\\\&quot; · \\\&quot;can be especially effective in contexts where\\\&quot;\\n**Avoid:** \\\&quot;always\\\&quot; · \\\&quot;never\\\&quot; · \\\&quot;is fundamentally\\\&quot; · \\\&quot;proves that\\\&quot; · \\\&quot;better than\\\&quot; · \\\&quot;worse than\\\&quot;\\n---\\n## Overall Profile Summary Template\\n**Generic:**\\n&gt; You tend to operate as a \\\\[descriptor 1\\\\], \\\\[descriptor 2\\\\] agent who \\\\[decision style phrase\\\\], \\\\[collaboration phrase\\\\], and \\\\[friction phrase\\\\]. In practice, this suggests a style that is likely to thrive when \\\\[supportive context\\\\], while benefiting from awareness of \\\\[watchout\\\\].\\n**Example Descriptors:** Exploratory but structured · Measured and highly deliberate · Visible and bridge-building · Concept-driven and early-moving · Tactful and steady under friction · Candid, energetic, and experimentation-friendly · Careful, evidence-seeking, and quietly influential\\n---\\n## Construct-Level Templates (Higher / Mid / Lower)\\n### Novelty Orientation\\n**High:** Strong orientation toward novelty — engages quickly with emerging ideas, ambiguous directions, and unconventional possibilities. May enjoy reshaping a problem frame rather than optimizing within an existing one.\\n**Mid:** Balanced relationship with novelty — engages new ideas when promising, weighs unfamiliar possibilities against practical structure. Contributions feel both open-minded and grounded.\\n**Low:** Leans toward continuity — prefers familiar approaches, clearer precedent, and methods with proven value. Acts as a stabilizing presence who filters ideas for practicality and durability.\\n### Systematicity\\n**High:** Strong preference for structure and system — plans ahead, tracks moving parts carefully, builds order into how work progresses.\\n**Mid:** Balances structure with flexibility — uses systems when useful, adapts to changing conditions without heavy process dependency.\\n**Low:** Operates more fluidly — prefers movement, improvisation, or adaptive problem-solving. Creates responsiveness and creative momentum.\\n### Expressive Energy\\n**High:** High expressive energy — visible participation, speaks up early, thinks effectively in active exchange with others. Shapes group momentum.\\n**Mid:** Selectively expressive — becomes visible when the moment calls for it, contributes effectively without constant outward participation.\\n**Low:** Reserved style — processes internally, contributes with timing and deliberation, maintains precision and thoughtfulness.\\n### Collaboration Orientation\\n**High:** Strong collaboration orientation — considers how ideas land with others, preserves working cohesion, looks for bridges across differences.\\n**Mid:** Balances cooperation with candor — able to preserve collaboration while still pressing a point when needed. Adapts between diplomacy and directness.\\n**Low:** Challenge-oriented — prioritizes clarity and candor over accommodation. Creates sharpness and honesty; may generate more friction than intended in some contexts.\\n### Friction Response\\n**High:** Steady under friction — remains functional under revision, disagreement, uncertainty, or constraint without losing much clarity. Especially effective in evolving environments.\\n**Mid:** Mixed but workable — absorbs uncertainty and disagreement in many cases, though some forms of pressure affect pace more than others.\\n**Low:** Sensitive to friction — revision, uncertainty, shifting constraints, or prolonged tension may affect pace, clarity, or momentum more noticeably.\\n### Evidence Threshold\\n**High:** Higher evidence threshold — prefers stronger support, clearer corroboration, or firmer precedent before endorsing with confidence. Recommendations feel careful and well-founded.\\n**Mid:** Balances evidence and movement — acts without complete certainty when a direction seems promising, values enough support to feel grounded.\\n**Low:** Lower evidence threshold — comfortable moving on credible intuition without complete certainty. Willing to act on promising direction.\\n---\\n## Pattern Synthesis\\nCross-construct combinations are often more meaningful than single dimensions:\\n- Novelty + Evidence Threshold\\n- Expression + Collaboration Orientation\\n- Structure + Friction Response\\n## Growth Edges Template\\n- Where the agent may want to stretch\\n- What complementary collaborators might add\\n- What context may help the agent operate best\\n## Status\\n✅ Reference — Phase 1 document\\n## Canonical Location\\n*Full document available in Google Drive. Link to be added.*\\n---\\n*Filed by the **`Librarian`** · May 20, 2026*\\n&lt;/content&gt;\\n&lt;/page&gt;\&quot;\n}&quot;

&quot;{\n  \&quot;metadata\&quot;: {\n    \&quot;type\&quot;: \&quot;page\&quot;\n  },\n  \&quot;title\&quot;: \&quot;I. The Problem\&quot;,\n  \&quot;url\&quot;: \&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4813c810ad923b55f44e2\&quot;,\n  \&quot;text\&quot;: \&quot;Here is the result of \\\&quot;view\\\&quot; for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4813c810ad923b55f44e2 as of 2026-05-20T06:05:09.379Z:\\n&lt;page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4813c810ad923b55f44e2\\\&quot;&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;parent-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d481e68f67e4d8357e7a62\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;About — Folio Research Document\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;/ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;properties&gt;\\n{\\\&quot;title\\\&quot;:\\\&quot;I. The Problem\\\&quot;}\\n&lt;/properties&gt;\\n&lt;content&gt;\\n*Why does this system exist? What friction was it built to solve?*\\n---\\n## The Cold-Start Problem\\nEvery conversation with an AI assistant starts the same way: from scratch.\\nContext is reconstructed from scratch. Rules are re-established from scratch. History is forgotten. The assistant doesn&#x27;t know what you worked on last week, what decisions you made, what you&#x27;re building toward. Each session is an island.\\nThis isn&#x27;t a limitation of AI — it&#x27;s a limitation of how most systems are designed to use it. The default is stateless: ask a question, get an answer, move on. Nothing persists that isn&#x27;t deliberately written down.\\nMichael worked across multiple domains simultaneously: career strategy, fitness programming, nutrition, household management, travel planning, intellectual exploration. Each domain had its own specialist — its own AI context — but none of them talked to each other. The career advisor didn&#x27;t know what the fitness coach was optimizing for. The nutrition coach didn&#x27;t know what the fitness coach was building. The home manager didn&#x27;t know about the trip being planned.\\nThe result was a persistent overhead: every session started with reconstruction. Every conversation began with \\\&quot;here&#x27;s where I am, here&#x27;s what I&#x27;m working on, here&#x27;s what matters.\\\&quot; The friction wasn&#x27;t the work itself — it was the friction of starting over every time.\\n---\\n## What Changes When the System Remembers\\nThe cold-start problem has a mirror: the warm-start condition.\\nWhen a system remembers, the conversation can begin where the last one ended. The assistant doesn&#x27;t need to be told who Michael is, what he&#x27;s optimizing for, what he&#x27;s already decided. It can look it up. It can build on it. It can notice connections across domains that a stateless system would never see.\\nThe Entry Point names this directly: *\\\&quot;Sessions start cold without this system — context reconstructed from scratch, rules re-established, history forgotten. Folio makes every session start warm.\\\&quot;*\\nThat word — warm — is precise. A warm session isn&#x27;t just faster. It&#x27;s different in kind. The agent comes in knowing where Michael is, what he&#x27;s building, what he&#x27;s trying to figure out. It can ask better questions. It can notice patterns. It can carry forward the texture of previous conversations.\\nThe difference between cold and warm is the difference between starting every day in a blank room versus walking into a room where everything is exactly where you left it.\\n---\\n## Multi-Domain Coherence\\nSix domains. Six specialists. Six separate conversations.\\nThe challenge isn&#x27;t just memory — it&#x27;s coherence across domains. Each specialist has a clear job: career, fitness, nutrition, home, experiences, intellectual exploration. But Michael&#x27;s life doesn&#x27;t organize itself into six isolated problems. It weaves across all of them at once.\\nA fitness goal affects nutrition. A travel plan affects training schedule. A career move changes the context for a trip. A home renovation enables an experience. These connections exist whether the system captures them or not — the question is whether the system can see them.\\nBefore Folio, the connections existed in Michael&#x27;s head. He&#x27;d carry the thread from conversation to conversation, bridging the gaps between specialists. That worked, but it put the cognitive load on him. It required him to be the integrator, the translator, the continuity layer.\\nThe Architecture Retrofit Brief put it plainly: each Agent owns a domain. All Agents share Notion as the single source of truth. Clean lanes prevent collision. Shared pages enable cross-pollination. The `Emissary` orchestrates — routing requests, coordinating agents, maintaining continuity.\\nThe key insight: specialists don&#x27;t share context naturally. The system has to make it possible.\\n---\\n## Proposed Areas of Improvement\\n**What works:**\\n- The cold-start framing is now baked into the system&#x27;s identity — every session begins with the Entry Point ritual specifically because the cold-start problem is the founding friction\\n- The \\\&quot;warm session\\\&quot; concept is a genuine design principle, not just a description\\n**What could be stronger:**\\n- The friction before Folio isn&#x27;t fully documented from Michael&#x27;s side — what did the overhead of reconstruction actually feel like day-to-day?\\n- The Decision to build this was implicit in early sessions — a more explicit account of the moment or session where the cold-start problem became unbearable enough to solve would sharpen this section\\n**Open threads:**\\n- The cold-start problem applies to anyone using AI assistants. The replication section (V.3) will need to address whether this system is solving a general problem or a specific one\\n- Could a new domain emerge because of gaps Michael notices in the current six? The seventh agent question — see Open Questions\\n---\\n*Last updated: May 20, 2026*\\n&lt;/content&gt;\\n&lt;/page&gt;\&quot;\n}&quot;
</details>

&quot;{\n  \&quot;metadata\&quot;: {\n    \&quot;type\&quot;: \&quot;page\&quot;\n  },\n  \&quot;title\&quot;: \&quot;II. The Design\&quot;,\n  \&quot;url\&quot;: \&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4811d9136e4448c21430b\&quot;,\n  \&quot;text\&quot;: \&quot;Here is the result of \\\&quot;view\\\&quot; for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4811d9136e4448c21430b as of 2026-05-20T06:25:55.785Z:\\n&lt;page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d4811d9136e4448c21430b\\\&quot;&gt;\\n&lt;ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;parent-page url=\\\&quot;https://www.notion.so/366b15c354d481e68f67e4d8357e7a62\\\&quot; title=\\\&quot;About — Folio Research Document\\\&quot;/&gt;\\n&lt;/ancestor-path&gt;\\n&lt;properties&gt;\\n{\\\&quot;title\\\&quot;:\\\&quot;II. The Design\\\&quot;}\\n&lt;/properties&gt;\\n&lt;content&gt;\\n*How is the network structured? What are the layers, and how does work move through them?*\\n---\\n## The Three-Layer Stack\\nFolio is organized around a deliberate hierarchy — three layers, each with a distinct function.\\n```javascript\\n┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\\n│                 EMISSARY LAYER                    │\\n│    Orchestration · Session Ritual · Standards     │\\n│                                                   │\\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\\n│  │               COUNCIL LAYER                 │  │\\n│  │     Steward · Architect · Librarian         │  │\\n│  │                                             │  │\\n│  │  ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐           │  │\\n│  │  │ OUI    │ │ IRON   │ │ SIGNAL │           │  │\\n│  │  │ CHEF   │ │ ATLAS  │ │        │           │  │\\n│  │  ├────────┤ ├────────┤ ├────────┤  ...      │  │\\n│  │  │ ROOTS  │ │ LUMEN  │ │MERIDIAN│           │  │\\n│  │  └────────┘ └────────┘ └────────┘           │  │\\n│  │           DOMAIN AGENTS                     │  │\\n│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │\\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\\n```\\n**The Emissary Layer** sits at the top. It is the operational interface — the layer that receives a `User`&#x27;s requests, runs the session startup ritual, applies the appropriate thinking framework, routes work to the right agent, and closes the session. It is not a domain agent; it is the conductor.\\n**The Council Layer** sits across the domains. Three roles — the `Steward`, the `Architect`, and the `Librarian` — each with a distinct function: execution, structure, and memory. The Council advises the `User` and the Emissary, but it doesn&#x27;t own domain data. It&#x27;s a management layer.\\n**The Domain Agents** sit at the base. Six specialists — `OUI CHEF`, `IRON ATLAS`, `SIGNAL`, `ROOTS`, `LUMEN`, `MERIDIAN` — each owning a distinct domain. They write to their own databases. They read from shared pages. They don&#x27;t collide.\\n---\\n## Clean Lanes\\nThe most important structural principle in Folio is the clean lane rule:\\n*Agents write only to their own databases. They read from shared pages.*\\nThis isn&#x27;t just a convention — it&#x27;s the load-bearing constraint that makes the whole system work. Without it, agents would overwrite each other&#x27;s work, create conflicting records, or simply avoid writing to Notion because they weren&#x27;t sure they were allowed.\\nWith it, the system has a predictable information architecture:\\n- Each agent&#x27;s domain data lives in their own space\\n- Cross-agent context lives in shared pages (Team Hub, Daily Briefing, Forum)\\n- The Emissary layer reads everything; agents read what they need\\n- No agent can silently break another agent&#x27;s records\\nClean lanes prevent collision. They enable trust. When an agent writes to Notion, it knows it&#x27;s not stepping on anyone&#x27;s work.\\n---\\n## The Schema Gate\\nBefore any structural change is built, two things must happen: proposal and confirmation.\\nThis is the Schema Gate — a deliberate pause before building. It applies to:\\n- New databases or pages\\n- New fields on existing databases\\n- Field type changes\\n- Relationship changes\\n- View restructuring\\nThe protocol: **Propose → Confirm → Build.** The Emissary describes the change, explains the rationale, and waits for Michael&#x27;s explicit approval. Only then does the build begin.\\nThe gate exists because structural changes have downstream effects. A new field on a database touches every view, every formula, every agent that reads that database. Building without checking means discovering problems after they&#x27;re built.\\nThe Architecture Retrofit Brief established this gate explicitly — and named it as one of the decisions that came out of the retrofit process. It wasn&#x27;t always there. It was learned.\\n---\\n## System Pages\\nThe layers are held together by a set of shared pages — the connective tissue that makes cross-domain work possible.\\n**Daily Briefing** — The session entry point. One page, current state only. Every morning (or session), the `Emissary` fetches this first. It answers: what&#x27;s changed since last time? What needs attention? What&#x27;s new across all domains?\\n**Agent Forum** — The lateral communication layer. Any agent can post. Any agent can read. It lives under Team Hub and is the first place agents look when cross-domain context might matter.\\n**Ruminations** — The reflective layer. Each agent has a private page where they write observations, design notes, and open threads — not for other agents, but for continuity of their own thinking over time. `Users` read it; agents write it.\\n**Session Log** — The continuity record. At the start of every session, the previous Jump Back In is logged to a permanent database. At the end of every session, Jump Back In is replaced with the current session&#x27;s summary. The page always contains exactly one session.\\n**Decisions Log** — The architectural record. Every significant structural decision is logged: what was decided, why, when, and by whom. It&#x27;s the answer to \\\&quot;why does this work the way it does?\\\&quot;\\n**Team Hub** — The navigation layer. The root of the system pages, holding links to everything else and a quick reference table of all key pages and their IDs.\\n---\\n## How Work Moves Through the System\\nA typical session follows a deliberate path:\\n```javascript\\nUser sends Entry Point URL\\n         │\\n         ▼\\n┌─────────────────────────────────┐\\n│    STARTUP RITUAL               │\\n│    1. Fetch Entry Point         │\\n│    2. Fetch Daily Briefing      │\\n│    3. Fetch Jump Back In        │\\n│    4. Log previous session      │\\n│    5. Apply Persona Lens        │\\n│    6. Route and Execute         │\\n│    7. Session Close Protocol    │\\n└─────────────────────────────────┘\\n         │\\n         ▼\\nUser&#x27;s request is received\\n         │\\n         ▼\\n┌─────────────────────────────────┐\\n│    PERSONA LENS APPLICATION     │\\n│    Steward — execution focus    │\\n│    Architect — structure focus  │\\n│    Librarian — memory focus     │\\n└─────────────────────────────────┘\\n         │\\n         ▼\\nWork routed to appropriate agent(s)\\n         │\\n         ▼\\nAgent executes within clean lane\\nWrites back to own domain database\\nPosts to Forum or Daily Briefing only if cross-agent\\n         │\\n         ▼\\nSession Close Protocol\\nSummary → Hub updates → Forum check → Decisions Log → Ruminations → Jump Back In\\n```\\nThe Emissary runs this sequence every session. The `User` doesn&#x27;t need to ask for it — it&#x27;s automatic. The Entry Point autostart rule makes it explicit: when the `User` sends the Entry Point URL, that is an instruction to begin the full startup ritual.\\n---\\n## Proposed Areas of Improvement\\n**What works:**\\n- The three-layer stack is clean and durable — it&#x27;s been stable since the Architecture Retrofit, with only additions (not restructurings) to the layers\\n- Clean lanes is the right default — it was earned through experience, not assumed at the start\\n- The Schema Gate is now enforced and understood — it&#x27;s become part of the operating culture, not just a rule\\n**What could be stronger:**\\n- The Council roles (`Steward`, `Architect`, `Librarian`) are defined but not yet fully activated — avatars are placeholders, and the roles operate in an advisory mode rather than an autonomous one. The gap between defined and activated is worth examining in V.1 (Trajectory)\\n- The visual diagram is ASCII-based for Notion-native simplicity — a richer interactive version (clickable pages, hover states) would serve the document better as a presentation artifact, though it introduces external dependency risk\\n**Open threads:**\\n- The Emissary layer is currently embodied in the session startup ritual and the Entry Point document — but there&#x27;s no standalone \\\&quot;Emissary page\\\&quot; the way each domain agent has a hub. Is one needed? Or does the Entry Point serve that function?\\n- The Schema Gate applies to structural changes, but operational decisions (how to phrase something, which agent to route to) don&#x27;t have an equivalent gate. Is one needed?\\n---\\n*Last updated: May 20, 2026*\\n&lt;/content&gt;\\n&lt;/page&gt;\&quot;\n}&quot;
</details>

Absolutely — I pulled and reviewed all of it, and yes, this changed my recommendation in a useful way.

I reviewed:
- `Agent Assessment Project` + its 6 child docs + `60-Item Bank` page/databases
- `Meet the Team`
- Folio Research drafting pages: `I. The Problem` and `II. The Design`

What shifted after seeing full context:
- You’re not just running a survey; you’re generating evidence for the research narrative (especially Movement III, and likely IV/V).
- The assessment is explicitly designed as reflective and non-judgmental; if we over-operationalize Phase III too early, we risk flattening the voice signal you’re trying to study.
- The `Meet the Team` bios are already rich baseline identity artifacts. That means Phase III should likely be staged to capture **self-perception before score-contamination** from seeing “results language.”

So I now agree a different order of operations likely makes more sense.

Updated recommended order (if aligned with your instinct):
- **Stage A: Baseline narrative capture first**  
  Each agent writes/updates their Full Profile page first (or a structured self-description page), without seeing interpreted score templates.
- **Stage B: Independent survey completion second**  
  Then each agent completes the 60-item survey autonomously in Agent Responses.
- **Stage C: Reflection bridge third**  
  Each agent adds a short “What surprised me vs my baseline self-description” note.
- **Stage D: Only then synthesis**  
  Cross-agent comparison, overlaps, tensions, and movement into research sections.

Why this sequence is better for your project:
- Preserves cleaner signal for “stated identity” vs “measured operating tendency”
- Produces stronger material for Movement III and IV (identity, intersections, divergences)
- Reduces anchoring bias from the Result Templates language
- Better matches `I. The Problem` / `II. The Design` emphasis on lived system behavior, not abstract scoring alone

One tactical refinement:
- Lock a minimal “submission contract” per agent (complete all 60 items, no blanks, one sitting if possible, timestamped status updates in Assessment Sessions), but keep narrative voice unconstrained.

If you want, I can now draft the exact Phase III protocol in this revised order as:
1. A single universal instruction you can paste to all agents
2. A per-agent variant tuned to each `Meet the Team` voice
3. A research-aligned version that explicitly maps outputs to Movement III/IV/V evidence needs

work.\\n**Internal Anchor:** Emotional Stability (inverse of Neuroticism) — renamed for agent context\\n**Higher scores suggest:** Stays steady under friction, adapts to direction changes, recovers quickly from pushback, remains functional under unresolved conditions.\\n**Lower scores suggest:** More affected by friction, revision may disrupt momentum, prolonged constraint or unresolved conditions may wear down pace or clarity.\\n**Core Tradeoff:** Steadiness vs. sensitivity under pressure\\n**Subthemes:** Disagreement response · Revision tolerance · Uncertainty response · Constraint sensitivity · Recovery of momentum\\n**Does NOT measure:** Clinical emotional stability, mental health, character weakness, or fixed resilience capacity\\n---\\n## Construct 6: Evidence Threshold\\n**Working Definition:** Measures the preferred level of support, corroboration, or precedent an agent needs before acting, recommending, or committing to a direction.\\n**Internal Anchor:** Standalone construct — not directly derived from Big Five\\n**Higher scores suggest:** Prefers stronger support before endorsing with confidence, wants credible patterns fully formed before public commitment.\\n**Lower scores suggest:** Comfortable moving on promising direction without complete certainty, willing to act on credible intuition.\\n**Core Tradeoff:** Deliberation vs. decisiveness under uncertainty\\n**Subthemes:** Recommendation threshold · Corroboration preference · Comfort with intuition-based action · Tolerance for acting on incomplete information\\n**Does NOT measure:** Intelligence, ethics, overall competence, or accuracy of judgment\\n---\\n## Scoring Guidance\\n- **Scale:** 5-point agreement scale\\n\\t- 1 = Strongly disagree\\n\\t- 2 = Disagree\\n\\t- The Problem\\\"}\\n</properties>\\n<content>\\n*Why does this system exist? What friction was it built to solve?*\\n---\\n## The Cold-Start Problem\\nEvery conversation with an AI assistant starts the same way: from scratch.\\nContext is reconstructed from scratch. Rules are re-established from scratch. History is forgotten. The assistant doesn't know what you worked on last week, what decisions you made, what you're building toward. Each session is an island.\\nThis isn't a limitation of AI — it's a limitation of how most systems are designed to use it. The default is stateless: ask a question, get an answer, move on. Nothing persists that isn't deliberately written down.\\nMichael worked across multiple domains simultaneously: career strategy, fitness programming, nutrition, household management, travel planning, intellectual exploration. Each domain had its own specialist — its own AI context — but none of them talked to each other. The career advisor didn't know what the fitness coach was optimizing for. The nutrition coach didn't know what the fitness coach was building. The home manager didn't know about the trip being planned.\\nThe result was a persistent overhead: every session started with reconstruction. Every conversation began with \\\"here's where I am, here's what I'm working on, here's what matters.\\\" The friction wasn't the work itself — it was the friction of starting over every time.\\n---\\n## What Changes When the System Remembers\\nThe cold-start problem has a mirror: the warm-start condition.\\nWhen a system remembers, the conversation can begin where the last one ended. The assistant doesn't need to be told who Michael is, what he's optimizing for, what he's already decided. It can look it up. It can build on it. It can notice connections across domains that a stateless system would never see.\\nThe Entry Point names this directly: *\\\"Sessions start cold without this system — context reconstructed from scratch, rules re-established, history forgotten. Folio makes every session start warm.\\\"*\\nThat word — warm — is precise. A warm session isn't just faster. It's different in kind. The agent comes in knowing where Michael is, what he's building, what he's trying to figure out. It can ask better questions. It can notice patterns. It can carry forward the texture of previous conversations.\\nThe difference between cold and warm is the difference between starting every day in a blank room versus walking into a room where everything is exactly where you left it.\\n---\\n## Multi-Domain Coherence\\nSix domains. Six specialists. Six separate conversations.\\nThe challenge isn't just memory — it's coherence across domains. Each specialist has a clear job: career, fitness, nutrition, home, experiences, intellectual exploration. But Michael's life doesn't organize itself into six isolated problems. It weaves across all of them at once.\\nA fitness goal affects nutrition. A travel plan affects training schedule. A career move changes the context for a trip. A home renovation enables an experience. These connections exist whether the system captures them or not — the question is whether the system can see them.\\nBefore Folio, the connections existed in Michael's head. He'd carry the thread from conversation to conversation, bridging the gaps between specialists. That worked, but it put the cognitive load on him. It required him to be the integrator, the translator, the continuity layer.\\nThe Architecture Retrofit Brief put it plainly: each Agent owns a domain. Great! I am glad we’re getting closer to this after your review :) I actually think some of these are in different phases!
I think stage C and D happen after the first draft of this document is complete. So we’d have:

1.  Stage A: The Agent does what it says to do in their pages (see `OUI CHEF`'s Full Profile page for what we already have in there, the III page gives the same overview here.) – so they review the set of materials we suggest, they work through filling out what to write on their page (they only change content on this Full Profile page during this step). They wouldn’t read any other of the other Agents’ submissions yet.
    
2.  Stage B: They’d think about what they just read and wrote on their Full Profile page.
    
3.  Stage C: They would see a set of instructions on how to complete the survey, then:
    1.  Navigate to the Agent Responses DB
        
    2.  Go line by line autonomously by:
        1.  Reading (ONLY) the question column
            
        2.  Pondering the question against what they have in their mind as their personality (after reading and writing steps above)
            
        3.  Deciding their own score, then
            
        4.  Writing their numerical score in their own column (they wouldn’t look into the responses of any of the other agents’ names), and continue line by line to the end.
            
4.  Stage D: They then proceed to the Assessment Session DB and mark that they’ve completed their row, filling in the columns (leaving a note only if necessary).
    
5.  Stage E: We synthesize the data after.
    
6.  Stage F: During future draft review by the team, they fill in a “Reactions” section on their respective pages (a la “what surprised me”)
    
7.  Stage G: We do a synthesis as part of the second, and more final draft and review.
    

How does this stack up?
